title: What Happens When You Don't Drink Enough Water?
description:
Send this to the friend whose only drink all day is coffee.
When you fall short on fluids, your brain releases a water-saving hormone (ADH) and your kidneys pull water back into your blood, so your pee turns dark yellow and strong-smelling (NHS, NIH). The NHS says to aim for 6 to 8 cups or glasses of fluid a day, and water, lower-fat milk and lower-sugar drinks, including tea and coffee, all count. Aim for pale yellow pee. If you already have dehydration symptoms, the NHS says to avoid caffeinated drinks and alcohol while you rehydrate. NHS: get urgent advice if you have dark yellow pee or you're peeing less than normal; call 999 (US: 911) if someone with signs of dehydration has blue, grey, pale or blotchy skin, lips or tongue, or is confused.
Next Body File: what happens when you hit snooze (that groggy fog has a name).
